purpose: Test whether the recurrent HOLD/EXIT failure in Request212 is partly caused by exact-minute trajectory semantics rather than by the position-state signal itself.
support_entry_policy: Request208 transition-relative recurrent ENTER/WAIT; used only to generate nonempty position trajectories for this structural HOLD/EXIT diagnostic because Request215 economically abstains on every development episode.
position_clock_rule: Re-anchor to the selected executable entry. Make HOLD/EXIT decisions only at later observed executable position states. Silent clock time implies forced HOLD/no action until the next observed state.
hold_target: Current-state HOLD advantage equals BASE return at the next actually executable observation minus BASE return from EXIT now.
causal_features: elapsed minutes since the previous observed event
stale minutes already elapsed before the current event
transition changes normalized by the already-observed previous event gap
outcome_only_fields: time until the next executable event
forbidden: using future next-event spacing as a model feature
treating unresolved held positions as cash
claiming Request208 support entries are the final end-to-end policy
comparison: Request208 fixed three-minute exit on identical support entries
